title: Strict Height-Balanced Invariants in a Chronos-Interpreter Parser: A Balanced Search Tree Approach
topic: The parser survey a USENIX paper left as future work
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: We present a rigorous analysis of a Chronos-Interpreter arithmetic parser that constructs a balanced binary search tree (BST) representation of the abstract syntax tree (AST). The parser enforces a strict height-balance invariant that guarantees $O(\log N)$ search, insertion, and rebalancing time for $N$ tokens. We formalize the invariant, prove its preservation under all parsing operations, and derive asymptotic bounds that match the theoretical limits of balanced BSTs \cite{Tarjan_1985_AmortizedComplexity}. The implementation is fully typed, uses a contiguous node layout, and is amenable to static verification. No empirical timing data is reported; all claims are supported by formal proofs and AST structural metrics. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/Chronos-Interpreter-advanced-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261104_200120_the_parser_survey_a_usenix_pap}
